newsitem.title: FRANCE: Promodes chief says family could cut stake.
newsitem.headline: Promodes chief says family could cut stake.

text.p: Promodes SA chairman Paul-Louis Halley said his family could envisage reducing its majority stake in the retailer to below 30 percent.
In an interview appearing in Friday's edition of Les Echos, Halley said his family, which controls Promodes, did not rule out a drop in its controlling shareholding.
"It wasn't that long ago, in 1989, that we had less than 30 percent of the capital...We can envisage returning to those percentage levels where we had been some 30 years."
An advance copy of the interview was sent to Reuters.
Halley also said he expected the French retail industry to consolidate, resulting in a market dominated by five big retail groups.

"In this country there will soon be five groups as in the other mature European markets. Look at Britain, look at what's going on in Germany. In all the countries with more than 50 million inhabitants, you find around five groups controlling between 65 percent and 80 percent of the market," Halley was quoted as saying.
Halley said Promodes continues to seek both internal and external growth.
But he said the group disliked hostile bids, much as it would have liked an alliance with Docks de France, recently taken over by rival Auchan.

"We have always mixed internal and external growth. We will continue," he said. "Recent history shows there are two ways to do it -- through friendly alliances or through an assault. I prefer the former."
He said Promodes had never launched a hostile takeover.
"I can tell you we would have been very happy to strike a friendly alliance with Docks de France. We tried to do so for a long time," he said.
Docks was acquired earlier this year by privately owned Auchan after failing to defend its independence.
Halley said the group aimed to expand outside France in a zone spanning Lisbon to Ankara. And from next year, it will begin to make substantial investments outside Europe.
"We'll go into fewer countries than some of our competitors, but in each case, we'll go in methodically, with the aim of capturing a significant position," he said.
Halley said the company regretted not having pulled out of Germany earlier, but expected its recent purchase for control of Italy's Gruppo G to generate "a significant source of revenue."
